title: A conditional reason or flag needs a test where the condition is false
rule: When code adds a reason, label or flag only under a condition (a score at or above a threshold, a model that weighs in, a rule that holds), test both sides on the same code path: one item that gets it and one item that passes every filter but must not get it. Build the input so the condition is clearly false (a hand-made model or fixture, not a lucky corpus value), and check the mutation `if true` fails the test. A test that only checks presence, or checks absence on a different path (the feature turned off), still passes when the guard is removed.
rationale: E33.2 (#197): the 'often paired in curated pairings' reason was tested only on a partner that should get it and on the rules-only path; replacing the probability guard with `if true` left every test green.
